title: Sample preparation protocol for hair fiber curvature analysis
author: Tina Lasisi
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bbweipbe
materials: The washing steps are taken to remove any products from the surface of the hair that may influence its longitudinal shape (aka. curl or curvature). The samples are set in a hot water bath to "revert" any changes to the hair due to extrinsic factors such as brushing, flat-ironing, braiding etc. Various tools and products used to alter hair texture/form work by breaking and reforming the (relatively weak) hydrogren bonds in the hair. Heat and moisture both break these bonds causing any artificially formed shape to the hair to be lost. There are limitations to this. Repeated styling over long periods of time may start influencing the structural integrity of the fiber beyond the flexible hydrogen bonds. Aditionally, any treatment affecting the disulfide bonds in the hair (e.g. perms) will not be undone by washing in hot water. As such, we recommend that researchers ask extensive questions about hair treatment history during hair sample collection, if they wish to study the intrinsic factors influencing hair morphology. Set aside materials for washing hairs The washing steps will require 500 µL of 1% SDS per hair in the sample batch (see comment and materials). 1.5 mL ddH2O per sample 1 mL IPA per sample An aspirator with replacement for each sample or a transfer pipette for each sample A (Vortex) mixer A pair of forceps A (Dryblock) water bath (with a thermometer) - this will need to be heated to 95 °C for use.

steps.title: Set up imaging station
steps.instruction: Set up a camera pointing down at an elevated stage with a white platform (e.g., a white sheet of paper).

steps.title: Transfer hairs to tubes
steps.instruction: Transfer cut hairs into 2mL tubes using a new transfer pipette for each sample.

substeps.instruction: Allow hairs to sink to the bottom between pipetting.
Pipette excess IPA from the 2mL tube to rinse the Petri dish and draw in more samples until most samples are in the tube.

steps.title: Prepare hair fragments
steps.instruction: Prepare a batch of 6 hairs for the protocol, ensuring a minimum of 5 hairs (around 30mm) per sample.

substeps.instruction: Place hairs onto a Petri dish filled with 5mL IPA.

steps.title: Dye lightly pigmented hairs
steps.instruction: If hair samples are lightly pigmented and not readily visible in the 2mL tube, dye them for better contrast before washing.

substeps.instruction: Prepare 10 mL of dye from a commercial dye kit in a 50mL Falcon tube according to kit instructions.
Remove most IPA from the 2mL tubes using an aspirator or transfer pipette without disturbing the hairs.
Add 1 mL of the mixed dye to each 2mL tube and let develop for a minimum of 00:30:00.
Rinse each tube with IPA, repeating the process until the liquid appears clear.

steps.title: Wash hairs with SDS
steps.instruction: Clean the hair samples using SDS solution.

substeps.instruction: Remove and discard as much IPA as possible using an aspirator or pipette without disturbing the hairs.
Add 500 µL 1% SDS solution.
Mix the contents using a Vortex mixer (do not turn the tube upside down).

steps.title: Heat and cool samples
steps.instruction: Apply heat treatment to the samples.

substeps.instruction: Place samples in a water bath heated to 95 °C for 00:05:00 (use cap locks to prevent caps from popping due to vapor pressure).
Remove hairs from the bath using forceps and place in trays to cool for at least 00:10:00.

steps.title: Centrifuge and rinse hairs
steps.instruction: Perform a series of centrifugation and rinse steps to clean the hairs.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge the cooled hairs at 10000 x g for 2 minutes.
Remove as much SDS solution as possible using an aspirator or pipette.
Fill the 2mL tube with 1.5 mL of ddH2O, mix using Vortex, and spin in a microcentrifuge at 10000 x g for 2 minutes.
Remove as much ddH2O as possible using an aspirator or pipette.
Add 1 mL of IPA to each sample and mix.

steps.title: Decant and image samples
steps.instruction: Prepare the hairs for macroscopic imaging.

substeps.instruction: Mix the contents of the 2mL tube and immediately decant into the Petri dish on the imaging stage.
If residual hairs remain in the tube, use a pipette to remove some IPA from the Petri dish and rinse the remaining hairs into the dish.
Capture the image of the hairs.
Dispose of hairs or retransfer them to 2mL tubes with 1 mL IPA for storage.
